sections.name: Mantis Blades
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm blades that count as melee weapons. They deal Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to cause bleeding.
Uses: You can leap at enemies in range for a big hit. Each Reflexes point adds 0.5% damage with them.
Tips: Buy them at a Ripperdoc once you hit level 10; quality rises every 10 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

sections.name: Monowire
sections.card:
Summary: Arm cyberware that deals Physical damage, with a 10-20% bleed chance and 0.5% more damage per Intelligence point.
Uses: Its empty slot takes a Control quickhack once you unlock the Jailbreak Relic perk. Charged attacks upload that quickhack to whatever they hit.
Tips: Ripperdocs sell it from level 10; quality rises every 10 levels and tops out at Tier 5. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

sections.name: Projectile Launch System
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that launches explosive projectiles.
Uses: Charge a shot for 30% more damage, 25% more explosion radius and 40% more dismember chance. Each Technical Ability point adds 0.5% damage.
Tips: Ripperdocs sell it from level 10, and quality rises every 5 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

sections.name: Gorilla Arms
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that counts as a blunt melee weapon. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to cause bleeding.
Uses: Fight in melee with them; each Body point adds 0.5% damage.
Tips: Ripperdocs sell them from level 10, and quality rises every 10 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

sections.name: Smart weapons
sections.card:
Summary: Smart weapons steer their bullets onto targets by themselves, but only with the Smart Link cyberware.
Uses: Keep the target inside the gun's tracking box. Shots bend around obstacles but fly slower than normal, and you cannot fit a suppressor or scope.
Tips: Smart Link (Hands) adds 10-20% target-lock duration and 5-15% crit damage for Smart weapons from Tier 3. Against Tyger Claws, smart shots miss 50% of the time because of their Masking Ink tattoos.

sections.name: Tech weapons
sections.card:
Summary: Railgun-style guns whose shots are driven by an electromagnetic charge.
Uses: Charge a shot so it passes through obstacles. Perks for them live under Technical Ability, and using Tech weapons trains the Engineer skill.
Tips: You cannot attach a suppressor to a Tech weapon, but most let you add a custom sight.

sections.name: Cyberdeck
sections.card:
Summary: Your Neuroport takes this datashard, which is what lets you quickhack and run Breach Protocol. Without a deck you cannot start Breach Protocol.
Uses: Quickhacks spend RAM. Buffer size caps the Code Matrix characters you can pick in Breach, and better decks have bigger ones.
Tips: Spent RAM returns after 60 seconds outside combat. Quickhacking perks and Frontal Cortex cyberware change your RAM, and resistant enemies cost more to hack.

sections.name: MaxDoc and Bounce Back
sections.card:
Summary: Two healing consumables: the Trauma Team MaxDoc inhaler and the Bounce Back injector.
Uses: The MaxDoc heals 50-126 Health when used. The Bounce Back heals 10-30 at once, then 6-17 more every second for 10 seconds.
Tips: You can find both in caches and on enemies. Vendors sell the MaxDoc, Meds Vendors sell the Bounce Back, and your inventory stacks them to 150.

sections.name: Enemies with Kerenzikov or a Sandevistan
sections.card:
Summary: Kerenzikov and Sandevistan are abilities some enemies have, and Sandevistan comes in Mk.1, Mk.2 and Mk.3.
Tips: The Wraiths' Revenant (fast melee) has Kerenzikov and Sandevistan Mk.1; a Kang Tao sniper has a Sandevistan. MaxTac officers use Sandevistan Mk.3 and Kerenzikov.

sections.name: Enemy netrunners
sections.card:
Summary: Enemy netrunners use quickhacks. The Voodoo Boys Netrunner (Tier 2) uses Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics, Ping and Overheat.
Tips: Overheat is a combat quickhack that ignites its target and keeps hurting it with Thermal damage. The Voodoo Boys Netrunner also carries EMP grenades and drops Tier 2 to Tier 5 quickhack components.

sections.name: Robots, mechs and drones
sections.card:
Summary: Robots, mechs and drones always have to be destroyed. Human foes can be subdued without killing them.
Tips: An enemy's icon colour shows its threat: white or grey is very low, and red is very high.

sections.name: Tyger Claws
sections.card:
Summary: One of Night City's largest gangs, based in Japantown but also holding ground in Westbrook and Watson.
Looks like: Glowing tattoos and katanas mark them out.
Tips: Their Masking Ink tattoos make smart-weapon shots miss 50% of the time. Its Hunter is a melee enemy at Tier 2; the gang also uses reflex boosters and pain editors.

sections.name: Maelstrom
sections.card:
Summary: A boostergang controlling much of Watson's Northside Industrial District. Its Goon (ranged or melee) and Ironstormer (heavy ranged) are both Tier 2.
Looks like: Chrome-heavy bodies and occult-style tattoos, looking more machine than human.
Tips: Ranged Goons carry frag grenades. The Ironstormer also wears Medium Subdermal Armor.

sections.name: Scavengers
sections.card:
Summary: Scavs kidnap people and take their cyberware by force. You can meet them all over Night City.
Looks like: Tracksuits and Soviet cyberware give them away.
Tips: Vultures are Tier 2 heavy ranged Scavs, equipped with frag grenades and Medium Subdermal Armor.

sections.name: MaxTac
sections.card:
Summary: The NCPD's cyberpsycho hunters come for you at five wanted stars, the last enemy type to do so. On higher difficulties a few shots can kill you at any level.
Tips: Squads have four officers, each in one of these roles: Assault, Mantis, Heavy, Netrunner or Sniper. Mantis officers have the second highest armor, and officers often use Sandevistan Mk.3 and Kerenzikov.
